question: A nurse throws an empty IV fluid bag with no blood stains into the regular office bin. Is this okay?

options.A: Yes, because it is general non-hazardous waste
options.B: No, intravenous items are always treated as sharps
options.C: No, all plastic items must go into infectious bins
options.D: Yes, provided the bag is shredded first by the nurse

explanation: Great choice! Clean packaging and IV bags that haven't touched blood or body fluids are safe to go into the general waste bin.

question: What is the main difference between static and dynamic balance?

options.A: Static equilibrium deals with head position at rest, while dynamic equilibrium responds to movement.
options.B: Static equilibrium uses the eyes only, while dynamic equilibrium uses the ears.
options.C: Static equilibrium controls heart rate, while dynamic equilibrium controls breathing.
options.D: Static equilibrium occurs only in water, while dynamic equilibrium occurs on land.

explanation: Think of it this way: static is staying still against gravity, while dynamic is when you are moving or turning around! [learn more](GNS211_U4_T8#GNS211_U4_T8_h1)

question: Which contraceptive method offers protection against both unintended pregnancy and sexually transmitted infections?

options.A: Lactational amenorrhea method
options.B: Progestin-only injectable pills
options.C: Male and female condoms
options.D: Combined oral contraceptive pills

explanation: Condoms act as physical barriers that prevent the exchange of body fluids, protecting against both pregnancy and infections. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T15#GNS324_U3_T15_h7)

question: In which part of our digestive system does most nutrient absorption happen?

options.A: Oral cavity
options.B: Stomach
options.C: Large intestine
options.D: Small intestine

explanation: You got it! The small intestine has tiny finger-like folds (villi) that create a huge surface area to soak up all the good nutrients into our bloodstream.

question: What is a key focus during post-test counselling for a client who tests negative?

options.A: Discussing prevention methods and the window period
options.B: Reporting the client to local security agencies
options.C: Isolating the client from their family members
options.D: Starting immediate lifelong antiretroviral treatment

explanation: Negative results require education on staying negative and understanding that recent exposures might not show up immediately during the window period. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T8#GNS216_U6_T8_h3)

question: What is the primary focus of public health nursing compared to traditional hospital bedside nursing?

options.A: Performing major surgical procedures independently
options.B: Prescribing advanced medications for rare conditions
options.C: Protecting and promoting the health of entire populations
options.D: Managing hospital budgets and medical equipment

explanation: Public health nursing looks past the single patient to protect whole communities and prevent illness at a macro level. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T17#GNS313_U1_T17_h1)

question: How long should a typical ergonomic micro-break last during a busy clinical shift?

options.A: 30 to 60 seconds
options.B: Half of the working day
options.C: 30 to 60 minutes
options.D: Exactly two hours

explanation: Correct! Even super short, frequent pauses are enough to shake off muscle tension without slowing down your patient care. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h7)

question: Which option best describes a holistic psychiatric care plan?

options.A: Combining medical treatment with lifestyle and complementary interventions
options.B: Treating mental illness only through strict physical isolation
options.C: Relying solely on herbal remedies while avoiding all prescription drugs
options.D: Focusing exclusively on physical vital signs during hospitalization

explanation: Holistic care looks at the whole human being—blending modern medicine with healthy lifestyle choices and supportive therapies.

question: Which of these is NOT a typical sign of joint inflammation that nurses look for?

options.A: Pain when moving the affected limb
options.B: Stiffness, especially after resting
options.C: Normal skin color and cool temperature
options.D: Swelling around the joint area

explanation: Spot on! Inflamed joints are usually warm, red, swollen, and painful—not cool and normal-looking!

question: Which of these is an example of a biological workplace hazard?

options.A: Loud machinery noise
options.B: Repetitive typing motion
options.C: Toxic cleaning solvents
options.D: Hepatitis B virus

explanation: Biological hazards come from living things like germs, bacteria, and viruses (such as Hepatitis B) that can affect healthcare workers and others. You're doing great!

question: Where are the internal female reproductive organs primarily located?

options.A: Inside the abdominal cavity
options.B: Within the true pelvis
options.C: Within the perineal body
options.D: Along the lower spinal canal

explanation: These organs are housed securely inside the bony true pelvis, which protects them from external trauma. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T2#GNS121_U5_T2_h1)

question: What is your immediate action if the patient feels sharp pain while you are flushing their ear?

options.A: Push the syringe faster to clear the blockage
options.B: Lower the temperature of the water
options.C: Stop the irrigation procedure right away
options.D: Ask the patient to lie flat on the bed

explanation: Pain is a warning sign of injury! Stop immediately to protect your patient from further harm. You're doing great learning this.

question: What is the main difference between privacy and confidentiality in research?

options.A: Privacy relates to blood samples, while confidentiality is for interviews
options.B: Privacy is a person's right to control their space, while confidentiality is our duty to protect their data
options.C: Privacy is optional, but confidentiality is required by law
options.D: Privacy applies only to doctors, while confidentiality applies to nurses

explanation: Spot on! Privacy belongs to the patient's personal boundaries, while confidentiality is our professional promise to keep their secrets safe.

question: What happens during exposure to a superantigen?

options.A: A complete shut down of all antibody production in the bone marrow
options.B: A slow and delayed immune response that lasts for several months
options.C: The immediate destruction of every circulating red blood cell
options.D: A massive and uncontrolled activation of a large percentage of T-cells

explanation: Superantigens bypass normal checks and balances, setting off a chaotic alarm that activates way too many T-cells at once.

question: Which chemical is mainly responsible for opening up blood vessels during inflammation?

options.A: Pepsin
options.B: Thyroxine
options.C: Histamine
options.D: Insulin

explanation: When tissues get hurt, mast cells release histamine. This chemical widens local blood vessels so helpful immune cells can rush to the rescue.

question: What is the main purpose of doing a 'test of change' in a healthcare setting?

options.A: To conduct a massive clinical trial on new surgical equipment
options.B: To try out a new idea on a small scale before full implementation
options.C: To permanently rewrite the national nursing practice guidelines
options.D: To punish staff who fail to follow standard hospital operating procedures

explanation: A test of change simply means trying out a new workflow or idea on a small scale first. It lets your team experiment safely without turning the whole hospital upside down!

question: What exactly is metabolism?

options.A: The rate at which the heart pumps blood to tissues
options.B: The total amount of water lost through skin and urine
options.C: All the chemical reactions that occur within the body
options.D: The physical process of digesting food in the stomach

explanation: Think of metabolism as the master umbrella for every chemical process happening in your cells to keep you alive and kicking. You've got this!

question: During patient assessment, which finding strongly suggests an underlying immune deficiency?

options.A: A sudden increase in energy levels and appetite
options.B: Localized itching from a minor insect bite
options.C: A single episode of mild seasonal influenza
options.D: Recurrent, severe, and unusual infections that do not respond well to standard treatment

explanation: Well done! A healthy body shakes off normal infections easily, but repeated or stubborn infections are a big red flag for immune breakdown.

question: As a nurse, what is one of the best ways you can help stop drug resistance?

options.A: Administering broad-spectrum drugs for every common viral cold
options.B: Educating patients to finish their entire antibiotic prescription
options.C: Stopping medication immediately once mild symptoms disappear
options.D: Encouraging patients to save leftover pills for future sickness

explanation: You got it! Always remind patients to complete their meds. Stopping early leaves the toughest germs alive to breed stronger, resistant generations.

question: How are most deep placental problems, like placenta accreta, usually spotted before delivery?

options.A: Measuring maternal blood pressure twice daily
options.B: Performing a routine digital cervical examination
options.C: Routine antenatal ultrasound and color Doppler imaging
options.D: Testing maternal blood hormone levels every week

explanation: Ultrasound with Doppler scans lets doctors look right at how the blood vessels are behaving before labor even starts. No guesswork needed! [learn more](GNS121_U6_T6#GNS121_U6_T6_h6)

question: Why is visiting a patient's home so helpful for disease management?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need for any medications.
options.B: It guarantees that the patient will never need a hospital visit.
options.C: It allows nurses to observe real-world habits and living conditions.
options.D: It places the entire workload on family members instead.

explanation: You get a true picture when you see where patients actually live! Home care lets you spot daily habits and environmental factors that directly affect their health.

question: Why must mast cell stabilizer sprays or drops be used regularly *before* an allergy season starts?

options.A: They interact with stomach acid if taken after an allergic attack starts.
options.B: They prevent cell rupture proactively but cannot reverse a reaction already underway.
options.C: They build up a thick physical barrier inside the nose that blocks dust.
options.D: They take at least two full weeks to enter the bloodstream for the first time.

explanation: Exactly! Think of them as prevention champs—they stop cells from popping, but they can't clean up the mess if the histamine has already spilled out.

question: What chemical signal do growing tumors release to tell new blood vessels to grow?

options.A: Insulin-like growth hormone
options.B: Vascular endothelial growth factor
options.C: Red blood cell stimulating protein
options.D: Platelet aggregation factor

explanation: VEGF is the chemical helper tumors use to build their own private highway system of blood vessels (angiogenesis).

question: What is a major feature of our innate immune system?

options.A: Slow and highly targeted
options.B: Dependent on prior exposure
options.C: Exclusive to viral infections
options.D: Rapid and non-specific

explanation: Innate immunity acts immediately! It doesn't need to 'remember' a past infection; it fights back right away using the same general tactics every time.

question: Why can relying too much on assistive technology become a problem in patient care?

options.A: It can reduce human interaction and lead to patient isolation
options.B: It automatically cures all chronic illnesses within days
options.C: It forces patients to perform rigorous physical exercises
options.D: It eliminates the need for any future medical research

explanation: You're doing great! While tech is helpful, leaning on machines too much can cut down on the warm, meaningful human contact patients need.

question: What usually happens to public health funding when the national economy goes through a tough patch?

options.A: Private clinics take over all public patients
options.B: Hospitals receive a sudden surge of extra grants
options.C: The cost of medical care drops to zero everywhere
options.D: Government health budgets are often reduced

explanation: Spot on. When money is tight nationally, governments collect less revenue and unfortunately tend to slash public sector budgets, including healthcare.

question: What is a major risk when international donors fund specific health programs?

options.A: They may ignore broader, foundational healthcare needs
options.B: They always cause the complete closure of local hospitals
options.C: They force nurses to stop practicing traditional methods
options.D: They remove all need for government budgeting

explanation: Donor funding often comes with strict conditions targeting single diseases, which can distract from overall health system strengthening. [learn more](GST321_U6_T3#GST321_U6_T3_h3)

question: Why is it important for you as a nurse to understand how drugs act at the cellular level?

options.A: To manufacture new pharmaceutical compounds in the ward
options.B: To bypass the need for regular patient vital sign checks
options.C: To anticipate both healing effects and unwanted side effects
options.D: To eliminate the requirement for physician prescriptions

explanation: Knowing how drugs work helps you stay one step ahead! It allows you to predict how the medicine will help your patient, and also watch out for any unexpected side effects.

question: How long should a nurse stay right by the patient's side after a blood transfusion starts?

options.A: Only until the pump is turned on
options.B: The first 15 minutes
options.C: Until the entire bag is empty
options.D: The first two hours

explanation: Most serious transfusion reactions happen fast at the very beginning. Staying close for those first 15 minutes lets you catch and treat any reaction early!

question: In basic microbiology, what exactly is an infectious agent?

options.A: A genetic trait passed down from parents
options.B: An environmental toxin found in polluted water
options.C: A vitamin deficiency that harms the immune system
options.D: Any microorganism capable of causing disease

explanation: You've got this! An infectious agent is simply any tiny germ—like a bacterium, virus, or fungus—that can get inside the body and cause illness.

question: A patient is moved from a rural clinic to a big city hospital with incompatible software. What is the biggest safety risk?

options.A: Critical allergy and medication history may be delayed or missing
options.B: Nurses will be forced to perform physical examinations outdoors
options.C: The patient room will lose electricity due to software overload
options.D: The patient will automatically be billed twice for their hospital stay

explanation: Spot on! When systems can't talk to each other, vital details like drug allergies can get lost in translation during transfers. Excellent clinical thinking!

question: Why must you wait for the alcohol swab on a vial stopper to air dry?

options.A: Drying is required for the alcohol to kill microorganisms effectively
options.B: It prevents the needle from slipping out of your fingers
options.C: Chemicals in wet alcohol deactivate the live vaccine virus
options.D: Wet alcohol ruins the rubber stopper and causes leaks

explanation: Alcohol needs a short amount of evaporation time to disrupt cell membranes and destroy bacteria on the rubber surface. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h3)

question: Why might a patient's surgical incision fail to heal properly due to poor diet?

options.A: The body lacks the necessary chemical building blocks for tissue repair
options.B: Patients who eat poorly refuse to take their prescribed painkillers
options.C: Dietary deficiencies completely stop blood circulation
options.D: Poor nutrition automatically causes surgical site infections

explanation: Cellular growth and tissue mending require specific nutrients like proteins and vitamins; without them, the body cannot effectively close wounds. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T001#GNS227_U2_T001_h1)

question: How do we mostly define a "community" in public health nursing?

options.A: A strictly administrative zone managed by the government
options.B: A collection of independent individuals living alone
options.C: A hospital ward filled with recovering patients
options.D: A dynamic social group with shared boundaries or interests

explanation: Think of a community as people connected by common ties, spaces, or goals—not just people living all by themselves. You've got this!

question: Which of these is NOT a typical result of eating a lot of junk food or processed snacks during adolescence?

options.A: Poor long-term bone health
options.B: Stronger skeletal bone density
options.C: Increased risk of iron deficiency
options.D: Erratic eating schedules

explanation: Processed foods lack key nutrients like calcium, so they certainly won't build stronger bones!

question: Why do red blood cells change into a sickle shape in this condition?

options.A: The bone marrow produces cells with too much iron and water inside them
options.B: Haemoglobin S molecules stick together to form rigid rods when they release oxygen
options.C: White blood cells attack and deform the healthy red blood cells
options.D: Excess sugar in the bloodstream causes the red blood cells to shrink and warp

explanation: When haemoglobin S delivers oxygen to body tissues, it clumps into stiff strands that distort the normal round cell into a crescent shape. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h1)

question: How do bilateral donor agencies typically help support healthcare in recipient countries?

options.A: By offering high-interest commercial loans exclusively to private doctors
options.B: By banning the importation of locally manufactured pharmaceutical drugs
options.C: By replacing the national ministry of health with foreign administrators
options.D: By providing direct grants and technical assistance for specific health programs

explanation: Bilateral agencies fund targeted health projects and share professional expertise to help build stronger local health systems.

question: Why is having a solid backup plan to a hospital so important for home birth programs?

options.A: Most women prefer to give birth in a hospital eventually
options.B: Emergency situations can develop unexpectedly during labor
options.C: Community health nurses are not allowed to deliver babies alone
options.D: Hospitals require proof of home birth for birth certificates

explanation: Childbirth can take sudden turns! That's why having a fast, reliable link to a hospital is a must-have safety net just in case complications pop up.

question: Which triage level requires immediate, life-saving intervention without any delay?

options.A: Routine outpatient level
options.B: Non-urgent level
options.C: Resuscitation level
options.D: Urgent level

explanation: Resuscitation is the highest triage level, meant for immediate life-threatening conditions like a stopped heart. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T1#GNS315_U2_T1_h2)

question: What is a major communication benefit of implementing MBO in a clinical setting?

options.A: It allows doctors to bypass nurses when giving patient orders
options.B: It completely replaces all written patient health records
options.C: It opens up constructive feedback channels between staff and management
options.D: It stops patients from complaining about hospital food

explanation: Structured check-ins give nurses a reliable voice to discuss operational roadblocks with directors. [learn more](GST321_U2_T5#GST321_U2_T5_h5)

question: Why is personalization considered a key principle in nutritional guidance?

options.A: Personalized diets guarantee that disease will never return
options.B: It allows nurses to charge higher fees for private consultations
options.C: Hospital regulations forbid giving the same diet to two different people
options.D: Generic advice often fails if it ignores a patient's budget and culture

explanation: If nutritional advice does not fit a person's real life, culture, and financial situation, they will not be able to follow it. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T001#GNS227_U7_T001_h3)

question: Why is it important to evaluate the primary caregiver during a home visit?

options.A: Caregivers are legally responsible for paying the nurse's salary
options.B: Caregivers often experience burnout and physical exhaustion
options.C: Caregivers usually have the same psychiatric diagnosis
options.D: Caregivers make all clinical decisions without medical advice

explanation: Family caregivers carry immense stress supporting a mentally ill relative, making their well-being a crucial focus of home care. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T6#GNS314_U4_T6_h4)

question: What happens when a nursing study uncovers surprising or unexpected findings?

options.A: The entire scientific community must stop investigating that topic
options.B: The study is immediately thrown away and hidden
options.C: Patients on the ward are taken off their medication
options.D: It opens the door for new research questions and follow-up studies

explanation: Spot on! Unexpected results are not failures; they challenge what we think we know and kick off the next round of helpful research.

question: What key lesson did the world learn from successful global vaccination campaigns against smallpox?

options.A: Coordinated international public health strategies can eradicate major diseases
options.B: Vaccines are only effective inside sterile hospital operating rooms
options.C: Local communities cannot participate in disease prevention
options.D: Infectious diseases disappear naturally without human intervention

explanation: Teamwork works! Smallpox proved that when the whole world joins forces on immunization, we can wipe out deadly diseases.

question: A peanut allergy patient feels completely fine 30 minutes after getting epinephrine and asks to go home immediately. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Perform allergy skin prick testing before allowing the patient to leave
options.B: Explain that prolonged observation is required to watch for secondary symptom flare-ups
options.C: Discharge the patient immediately with a prescription for oral antihistamines
options.D: Administer a second dose of epinephrine just to prevent any future problems

explanation: Don't let them rush off just yet! Because of the risk of biphasic reactions, patients need to stay in the hospital for observation for a few hours.

question: How does bovine mastitis (udder infection) directly affect raw milk?

options.A: It forces the cow to stop producing any milk permanently
options.B: It introduces pathogenic bacteria directly into the milk stream
options.C: It completely sterilizes the milk inside the udder gland
options.D: It increases the acid level enough to kill all other germs

explanation: Exactly! Mastitis means the cow's udder is infected, which unfortunately dumps disease-causing germs right into the milk as it's being produced.

question: What is the main biological goal of giving someone a vaccine?

options.A: To provide permanent physical barriers like thickened skin
options.B: To kill all normal flora bacteria residing in the gut
options.C: To stimulate memory cells without causing severe disease
options.D: To permanently disable the patient's innate immune response

explanation: Vaccines give your immune system a safe rehearsal. They train your adaptive memory cells so you're ready if the real germ ever shows up.

question: You check a mum on her 3rd day after birth. Where do you expect to feel her fundus?

options.A: Completely hidden in the pelvic cavity
options.B: About three fingerbreadths below the umbilicus
options.C: Level with the umbilicus
options.D: Midway between the pubic bone and umbilicus

explanation: You're learning fast! Since the uterus drops by about one fingerbreadth each day after birth, by day three it sits roughly three fingerbreadths below the belly button. Easy to remember on the ward!

question: Which ethical principle are you upholding when you give a patient honest, complete details about a drug's side effects?

options.A: Maleficence
options.B: Paternalism
options.C: Autonomy
options.D: Fidelity

explanation: Spot on! Autonomy is all about respecting the patient's right to make their own choices based on honest and clear information.

question: Why is a slightly lower hemoglobin level accepted during the second trimester?

options.A: Maternal bone marrow becomes temporarily suppressed
options.B: Red blood cell production completely stops temporarily
options.C: Greater plasma volume expansion occurs during this period
options.D: Fetal iron demands are lowest at this stage of growth

explanation: Spot on! The body makes a lot more fluid (plasma) during the second trimester. This extra fluid dilutes the red blood cells, which naturally lowers the hemoglobin reading without meaning she's losing blood.

question: What is the main goal of primary prevention when it comes to gender-based violence?

options.A: To treat physical injuries sustained during an attack
options.B: To prosecute offenders in a court of law
options.C: To provide emergency shelter after an assault
options.D: To stop violence before it ever occurs through education and awareness

explanation: You're doing great! Primary prevention is all about stopping violence before it even starts by teaching equality and healthy relationships.

question: At what heart rate should you start chest compressions during newborn resuscitation?

options.A: Below 60 beats per minute
options.B: Below 80 beats per minute
options.C: Below 40 beats per minute
options.D: Below 100 beats per minute

explanation: If the heart rate drops below 60 despite good assisted breathing, the heart needs direct chest compressions to keep blood flowing.

question: What is the first phase of the nursing process?

options.A: Diagnosis
options.B: Assessment
options.C: Planning
options.D: Evaluation

explanation: Assessment is always the starting point, where the nurse collects all necessary information about the patient. [learn more](GST319_U4_T2#GST319_U4_T2_h3)

question: Which of these is a non-pharmacological comfort measure a nurse can use during a disaster?

options.A: Intravenous morphine administration
options.B: Emergency surgical airway placement
options.C: Rapid blood transfusion
options.D: Gentle repositioning and reassuring communication

explanation: Spot on! Non-pharmacological means soothing the patient without drugs—using your nursing touch, kind words, and proper positioning to ease their distress.

question: A local health district has a fixed budget to build two new clinics. Based on primary health care principles, where should these clinics be built?

options.A: In affluent neighborhoods where residents can pay user fees
options.B: Inside the capital city near the main teaching hospital
options.C: In the most rural and underserved farming communities
options.D: Next to the regional airport for easy international access

explanation: Equitable distribution directs resources to areas with the highest need and least existing access, which are usually rural communities. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T5#GNS124_U1_T5_h3)

question: Why might health policies and laws look a bit different depending on which Nigerian state you are working in?

options.A: Due to regional differences in laws, culture, and state-level guidelines
options.B: Because nurses are only permitted to follow international laws
options.C: Because the federal government has no ministries dedicated to health
options.D: Due to a complete lack of any written healthcare policies in the country

explanation: Nigeria's federal system means local cultures and state laws can influence how national health guidelines are put into practice. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h3)

question: A patient is getting intravenous Amphotericin B for a severe kidney fungal infection. Which lab tests should you check most closely?

options.A: Platelet count and bleeding time
options.B: Liver enzymes and bilirubin levels
options.C: Serum sodium and potassium levels
options.D: Serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen

explanation: Because Amphotericin B is harsh on the kidneys, we always monitor kidney function markers like creatinine and BUN closely.

question: What is the primary fluid collected during a lumbar puncture?

options.A: Synovial joint fluid
options.B: Peritoneal lavage fluid
options.C: Cerebrospinal fluid
options.D: Pleural cavity fluid

explanation: A lumbar puncture specifically targets the subarachnoid space to draw cerebrospinal fluid for laboratory analysis. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T9#GNS221_U2_T9_h1)

question: Why should a home health nurse document environmental hazards like poor lighting or uneven floors?

options.A: These factors directly influence client safety and risk of injury
options.B: Insurance companies use this data to calculate property taxes
options.C: Building inspectors require nurses to enforce local housing laws
options.D: It proves the nurse inspected the neighborhood security system

explanation: Environmental conditions in a home directly impact clinical outcomes, such as increasing the risk of falls for an elderly client. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T6#GNS324_U2_T6_h4)

question: What is the very first thing to check if a patient's pulse oximetry reading suddenly drops during transport?

options.A: The vehicle's tire pressure and engine oil temperature
options.B: The patient's surgical history from three years ago
options.C: The exact mileage left before reaching the hospital gate
options.D: The physical connection of the sensor and monitor cable

explanation: Bumps and patient movement frequently displace monitoring probes, so checking equipment connections prevents false alarms. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T9#GNS315_U3_T9_h3)

question: What is a major health risk for a teenage athlete who consistently eats far fewer calories than their body burns?

options.A: Excessive increases in height growth
options.B: Instant muscle hypertrophy and strength gains
options.C: Delayed puberty and poor bone health
options.D: Improved long-term cardiovascular immunity

explanation: When growing teens don't get enough fuel, their hormone balance gets upset, which can delay puberty and weaken their bones.

question: A confused elderly patient keeps holding pills in their cheek without swallowing them. What is this behavior called?

options.A: First-pass effect
options.B: Pouching
options.C: Aspiration
options.D: Enteric coating

explanation: Pouching happens when patients store food or medication in their cheek pockets instead of swallowing it. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T14#GNS122_U1_T14_h6)

question: What is one of the primary frontline duties of a community health nurse during an outbreak?

options.A: Manufacturing vaccines in a laboratory setting
options.B: Managing international airport immigration desks
options.C: Tracing contacts and listing exposed individuals
options.D: Writing national health legislation and edicts

explanation: Community health nurses actively participate in contact tracing to identify and monitor those who need quarantine. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T5#GNS313_U2_T5_h9)

question: During which phase of the PDSA cycle do you actually carry out your new idea on a small scale?

options.A: Do phase
options.B: Act phase
options.C: Study phase
options.D: Plan phase

explanation: The 'Do' phase is where the action happens! You test your idea on the ward and see how it works in real life.

question: What is a common misconception about the health status of HIV orphans?

options.A: People assume all orphans are infected with HIV themselves
options.B: People assume orphans never require routine immunizations
options.C: People think orphans are immune to childhood malnutrition
options.D: People believe orphans cannot contract malaria or typhoid

explanation: Not every child who loses a parent to HIV has the virus. Many are negative and simply suffering from poverty and loss. Keep this distinction clear in your practice!

question: Why are nurses such valuable members of a quality improvement team?

options.A: They write hospital policy manuals alone
options.B: They have formal training in hospital finance
options.C: They make all final administrative decisions
options.D: They spend the most time at the bedside

explanation: Exactly! Because nurses are right there with patients every day, they see firsthand what works and where things go wrong in clinical care.

question: Which regional African treaty specifically calls for stopping and banning FGM?

options.A: The Abuja Declaration
options.B: The Lagos Health Accord
options.C: The African Union Charter on Trade
options.D: The Maputo Protocol

explanation: Well done! The Maputo Protocol focuses heavily on women's rights across Africa and requires member countries to outlaw FGM.

question: What is the safest way to move a heavy patient up in bed without hurting your back?

options.A: Twist your torso to shift the weight in a single smooth motion
options.B: Ask the patient to push with their legs while you lift alone
options.C: Bend sharply at the waist to pull the patient quickly
options.D: Use an overhead mechanical lift and get a second staff member

explanation: Spot on! Protect your back by using mechanical tools and asking a colleague for help. Nursing is teamwork!

question: Which group is usually eligible for DRF exemptions in our hospitals?

options.A: Elected political office holders
options.B: Employed corporate executives
options.C: Wealthy private business owners
options.D: Indigent elderly patients without support

explanation: Older adults who lack pensions or family financial backup are standard beneficiaries of these hospital welfare safety nets.

question: Which vital sign must you always check before giving a combined hormonal contraceptive?

options.A: Respiratory rate
options.B: Temperature reading
options.C: Blood pressure
options.D: Oxygen saturation

explanation: Always check BP first! Estrogen can push blood pressure up and increase heart risks in vulnerable clients.

question: What is the main job of descriptive statistics in nursing research?

options.A: To summarize and organize raw healthcare data
options.B: To prove a cause-and-effect relationship between drugs
options.C: To predict future disease outbreaks using probability
options.D: To test complex hypotheses with small sample sizes

explanation: You've got this! Descriptive statistics are simply tools to tidy up large piles of data, making it easy for us to see the main picture without getting bogged down in numbers.

question: You notice rising rates of malnutrition in a local village during your community posting. What is your best first step as a nurse?

options.A: Wait patiently in the health post until parents bring children in
options.B: Demand that international organizations take over food distribution
options.C: Collaborate with local leaders to educate families on using local food sources
options.D: Immediately shut down all local food markets until supplies improve

explanation: Working hand-in-hand with village leaders to teach healthy eating using available local foods is practical and sustainable!

question: What is the main goal of the DASH diet for someone with high blood pressure?

options.A: To increase potassium, calcium, and fiber while reducing sodium
options.B: To replace all fluid intake with specialized herbal teas
options.C: To encourage rapid weight loss through strict calorie counting
options.D: To eliminate all carbohydrates from the daily meal plan

explanation: DASH focuses on whole foods packed with good minerals like potassium and calcium while cutting back on salt to protect the heart.

question: Which chronic medical condition is a leading cause of peripheral neuropathy?

options.A: Iron deficiency anemia
options.B: Essential hypertension
options.C: Diabetes mellitus
options.D: Asthma

explanation: Long-term high blood sugar levels commonly damage peripheral nerves, making diabetes the most frequent cause of neuropathy. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T4#GNS211_U3_T4_h9)

question: How does the ongoing brain drain impact the nurses who decide to stay and practice in Nigeria?

options.A: They automatically receive double salaries from government funds
options.B: They are barred from attending professional nursing conferences
options.C: They must close down all public primary health centers
options.D: They face heavier workloads, burnout, and dangerous nurse-to-patient ratios

explanation: That's right. When colleagues leave, the remaining nurses have to pick up the slack, leading to severe exhaustion and stretched resources.

question: What is the most important instruction for a patient going home with oral antibiotics for salpingitis?

options.A: Only treat your partner if they develop a fever
options.B: Resume sexual activity immediately if you feel fine
options.C: Stop taking the pills as soon as your belly pain stops
options.D: Finish all the medication even if you start feeling better

explanation: Always remind patients to finish their full course of antibiotics so the infection doesn't bounce back stronger!

question: Which level of government is mainly responsible for funding general hospitals that provide secondary care?

options.A: Local government council
options.B: International donor agencies
options.C: Private voluntary organizations
options.D: State government

explanation: Great job! State ministries of health take charge of managing and funding general hospitals, which make up our secondary care tier.

question: A patient after an abortion has a weak, fast pulse, low blood pressure, and cold skin. What condition is she likely developing?

options.A: Uterine perforation
options.B: Hypovolemic shock
options.C: Postpartum depression
options.D: Pelvic inflammatory disease

explanation: Spotting these vital signs is a core nursing skill! A fast pulse, low BP, and cold skin tell us the body is running low on fluid volume due to heavy bleeding—classic hypovolemic shock.

question: What do we mean in healthcare when we say 'the physical environment creates the disability'?

options.A: Inaccessible buildings and transport disable people more than their actual medical impairment.
options.B: People with disabilities prefer staying indoors away from society.
options.C: Bad weather directly causes permanent physical paralysis.
options.D: Hospitals are solely responsible for causing new physical disabilities.

explanation: A person with a mobility challenge can thrive if buildings have ramps and elevators. Often, it's the lack of accessible infrastructure—not the body itself—that creates the barrier.

question: How do nurses help make hospitals safer against disasters?

options.A: By funding the construction of new earthquake-proof walls
options.B: By purchasing emergency generators with personal funds
options.C: By writing national environmental zoning policies
options.D: By serving on disaster committees and pointing out safety hazards

explanation: Spot on! Nurses use their daily ward experience to help planners catch and fix safety risks early.

question: A patient twists their ankle and cannot take four steps without severe pain. What is the best next step?

options.A: Assess for bone tenderness and prepare the patient for a possible X-ray
options.B: Apply a warm compress immediately to relax the joint muscles
options.C: Discharge the patient home with instructions for strict bed rest only
options.D: Massage the ankle firmly to check for deep ligament tears

explanation: When a patient can't bear weight after an injury, standard safety guidelines require checking for bone tenderness and getting an X-ray to rule out a fracture.

question: Why is community education and reducing stigma such a vital part of nursing care for immune conditions?

options.A: It encourages people to seek testing and treatment early without fear.
options.B: It stops patients from needing physical check-ups at the clinic.
options.C: It replaces the need for nutritional supplements in rural areas.
options.D: It lowers the cost of manufacturing hospital equipment.

explanation: Brilliant! When we break down stigma, patients feel safe to get tested and start life-saving treatment early.

question: Why is checking the publication date important when reading health articles online?

options.A: Older articles require special passwords to open them
options.B: Websites automatically delete articles after exactly one year
options.C: Older web pages take up too much space on computer screens
options.D: Medical guidelines and treatment practices change as new research emerges

explanation: Healthcare is fast-moving, and outdated information can lead to unsafe clinical practices or incorrect patient education. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T9#GNS113_U1_T9_h5)

question: What is the primary clinical use of oxybutynin?

options.A: Dilating airways in asthma
options.B: Increasing a slow heart rate
options.C: Treating overactive bladder
options.D: Preventing motion sickness

explanation: Oxybutynin relaxes the bladder muscle to reduce urinary urgency and frequency. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T6#GNS223_U5_T6_h3)

question: How does your skin play a vital role in keeping your bones strong with calcium?

options.A: By filtering calcium out through the sebaceous glands
options.B: By synthesizing vitamin D precursors using UV light
options.C: By storing dietary calcium directly in the epidermis
options.D: By producing specialized calcium-binding sweat

explanation: Fantastic! Sunlight hits the skin to jumpstart vitamin D production, which your gut needs to absorb calcium properly.

question: If a needle has a lower gauge number, what does that tell you about its size?

options.A: The needle length is shorter
options.B: The needle width is larger
options.C: The syringe barrel is smaller
options.D: The needle tip is sharper

explanation: Needle gauges can be tricky! Just remember: the smaller the gauge number (like 20G), the thicker and wider the needle is. A higher number (like 25G) is much thinner.

question: Why do we take off our gloves FIRST before removing other PPE items?

options.A: Gloves are usually the most contaminated items touched during care
options.B: Gloves are the only reusable item in the standard PPE set
options.C: Gloves interfere with untying the back of the protective gown
options.D: Gloves take the longest time to take off safely

explanation: Exactly! Your gloves have touched all the germs, so taking them off first stops you from accidentally smearing those pathogens onto your face or mask while undressing.

question: Who are considered key stakeholders when mobilizing a Nigerian community for a public health campaign?

options.A: Only the youngest children in the primary school
options.B: Foreign tourists visiting local wildlife parks
options.C: Traditional rulers, religious leaders, and local group heads
options.D: International manufacturing companies overseas

explanation: Spot on! Community and religious leaders hold massive influence over public participation. Working with them makes every health campaign smoother.

question: What is a key nursing action to prevent bedsores (pressure injuries) in immobile residents?

options.A: Applying strong antiseptic ointment to all bony areas
options.B: Limiting fluid intake to prevent skin moisture
options.C: Keeping the resident in bed twenty-four hours a day
options.D: Implementing regular repositioning schedules

explanation: Spot on! Turning and repositioning patients regularly takes the weight off bony spots, keeping their skin safe and healthy.

question: What should you do if a patient calls reporting sudden chest pain and severe shortness of breath?

options.A: Ask them to send a text message if the pain gets worse tomorrow
options.B: Tell them to wait until next week for a routine clinic appointment
options.C: Instruct them to immediately seek emergency medical care or transport
options.D: Advise them to drink warm water and sleep for an hour

explanation: Safety first! Chest pain and severe breathing trouble are red flags. They need immediate physical medical attention, not home management.

question: When is an autocratic leadership style most appropriate in a primary health care setting?

options.A: During a routine community health education meeting
options.B: During a sudden medical emergency or trauma resuscitation
options.C: When scheduling the monthly staff social gathering
options.D: When designing a new long-term clinic budget

explanation: Quick, direct orders without debate are essential in urgent medical emergencies to save time and prevent errors. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T13#GNS124_U5_T13_h3)

question: Why do nurses use a pH testing strip when checking a newly placed nasogastric tube?

options.A: To test how acidic the fluid pulled from the tube is
options.B: To check the expiry date of the food formula
options.C: To check if the patient has a stomach ulcer
options.D: To measure the sugar level in the feed

explanation: Stomach acid is very sour! Testing the pH of fluid from the tube helps us confirm the tip is safely inside the acidic stomach, not the lungs.

question: What is the main job of a 'cold chain' logistics system when moving food around?

options.A: Perishable items from spoiling by maintaining low temperatures
options.B: Dry grains from getting wet during heavy rain
options.C: Livestock from escaping transport trucks
options.D: Metal cans from rusting inside storage warehouses

explanation: A cold chain keeps a continuous refrigerator system going from the farm all the way to the store shelf so perishables stay fresh.

question: What is the main chemical difference between vitamins and minerals?

options.A: Vitamins contain heavy metal ions instead of carbon
options.B: Minerals are fragile organic compounds destroyed by cooking
options.C: Minerals are inorganic elements that lack carbon-hydrogen bonds
options.D: Vitamins are solid metallic rocks found naturally in soil

explanation: Correct! Minerals are pure elemental substances from the earth, while vitamins are complex organic molecules made by living things.

question: A community nurse is preparing to measure a toddler's MUAC. Where on the arm should the tape be placed to find the correct midpoint?

options.A: At the thickest part of the bicep muscle
options.B: Right below the armpit crease
options.C: Directly over the middle of the forearm
options.D: Between the shoulder tip and the elbow tip

explanation: You've got this! To get an accurate MUAC, always locate the exact midpoint between the shoulder (acromion) and the elbow (olecranon).

question: Aside from clinical health, what major factor shapes a person's family planning choices?

options.A: Global weather patterns
options.B: Hospital bed capacity
options.C: Socio-cultural dynamics
options.D: Local taxi fare rates

explanation: You nailed it! Family planning choices are deeply tied to cultural traditions, beliefs, and community values, not just pure medicine.

question: How does hospice philosophy view the dying process?

options.A: As an unpredictable event requiring intensive surgery
options.B: As a natural part of the human life cycle
options.C: As a condition that can always be reversed with therapy
options.D: As a medical failure that must be fought at all costs

explanation: Hospice care embraces dying as a normal stage of life rather than viewing it purely as a medical failure. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T14#GNS324_U5_T14_h2)

question: When a person experiences trauma, what does "somatization" mean?

options.A: A complete loss of memory regarding the traumatic event
options.B: Expressing emotional distress through physical bodily complaints
options.C: Sudden aggressive outbursts directed at rescue workers
options.D: An inability to speak while remaining fully conscious

explanation: You've got this! Somatization happens when emotional pain gets heavy and shows up physically—like unexplained headaches or stomach aches. The body speaks when words are too hard to find. [learn more](GNS314_U6_T3#GNS314_U6_T3_h2)

question: An infant is brought to the clinic for routine immunization at 9 months old. Which key vaccine is due at this visit?

options.A: Measles vaccine
options.B: Pentavalent booster dose four
options.C: First dose of BCG
options.D: Oral polio vaccine dose zero

explanation: Spot on! The first dose of the measles vaccine is scheduled right at 9 months to keep growing babies safe.

question: Which of these is an example of a research design rather than a tool?

options.A: A laboratory test tube used to check blood sugar
options.B: The overall structural framework of the study
options.C: A structured questionnaire handed to patients
options.D: An audio recording device used during an interview

explanation: Great job! The overall framework is your design, while items like questionnaires and test tubes are the physical tools you use inside that design.

question: During a community disease outbreak, what is the main cause of biological hazard emergencies?

options.A: Accidental leakage of industrial gas from factories
options.B: Sudden heavy rainfall flooding residential areas
options.C: Rapid spread of infectious diseases among populations
options.D: Widespread consumption of expired tinned foods

explanation: Biological hazards are living microscopic troublemakers like bacteria and viruses that spread fast through communities. Keep up the good work!

question: Why do patients with severe fluid overload often develop crackling sounds in their lungs?

options.A: Dehydration causes the bronchial tubes to narrow and whistle
options.B: Fluid backs up into the pulmonary air sacs and airways
options.C: The chest muscles weaken from holding extra body weight
options.D: The patient develops a secondary bacterial pneumonia infection

explanation: Spot on! When the plumbing system is overloaded, fluid backs up into the tiny air sacs (alveoli) in the lungs, making a crackling sound when they breathe.

question: Why is using good, clear logic so important from the beginning to the end of your research?

options.A: It guarantees the hospital will fund the research project
options.B: It ensures conclusions directly match the gathered evidence
options.C: It removes the need for any statistical calculations
options.D: It stops patients from withdrawing from the study

explanation: Spot on! Sound logic stops us from making wild claims that our actual data doesn't back up. Keep it logical!

question: Why do healthcare decisions often involve political negotiation?

options.A: Medical equipment never breaks down unexpectedly
options.B: Resources are limited and demand is high
options.C: Doctors refuse to speak with government officials
options.D: Patients prefer traditional healers to hospitals

explanation: Scarcity forces leaders to make tough choices about where money and support go, which requires political bargaining. [learn more](GST321_U6_T3#GST321_U6_T3_h1)

question: Which of these is a common reason a patient would need a laryngoscopy?

options.A: Severe abdominal pain
options.B: Persistent hoarseness
options.C: Lower leg swelling
options.D: High blood pressure

explanation: Well done! If someone's voice has been unusually rough or hoarse for a long time, doctors use a laryngoscopy to take a closer look at the vocal cords.

question: According to global health guidelines, how long should an infant be exclusively breastfed?

options.A: For the first six months of life
options.B: For the first three months only
options.C: Until the infant starts walking
options.D: Until the baby cuts their first tooth

explanation: Exclusive breastfeeding for the first six months gives babies the absolute best start, providing all the water, food, and immune protection they need!

question: Why do nurses compare data collected after a health campaign with the baseline numbers gathered before it started?

options.A: To satisfy personal curiosity about how many posters were printed
options.B: To determine if the health campaign actually caused positive behavior changes
options.C: To calculate the exact travel expenses of the visiting health team
options.D: To prove that no one in the community attended any health meetings

explanation: Spot on! Comparing 'before' and 'after' numbers is the only way to prove whether your awareness campaign truly made a difference.

question: What is the very first sign a nurse looks for on a growth chart to spot growth faltering?

options.A: A stable horizontal line that matches the birth weight
options.B: A sudden spike in height above the ninety-fifth percentile
options.C: A flattening or downward crossing of weight percentiles
options.D: An abrupt increase in head circumference beyond normal limits

explanation: Growth faltering happens quietly at first—the child stops gaining weight along their usual curve, causing the line to flatten or dip across the percentile tracks.

question: How does effective IEC help reduce the workload of overcrowded primary health clinics?

options.A: By convincing patients that they do not need to visit a nurse for minor symptoms
options.B: By automatically curing chronic diseases without the need for medication
options.C: By locking clinic doors on certain days of the week to force home remedies
options.D: By teaching people preventive habits and early care that stop mild illnesses from becoming severe

explanation: When communities practice prevention and seek early care, fewer people develop severe complications that require intensive clinic resources. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T2#GNS124_U5_T2_h2)

question: Why is daily foot care and inspection so crucial for patients with diabetes?

options.A: Daily observation increases blood circulation to the toes
options.B: Sweat buildup guarantees the rapid development of gangrene
options.C: Nerve damage can prevent them from feeling minor cuts or blisters
options.D: Skin color changes indicate the exact blood sugar level

explanation: Diabetes can cause nerve damage (neuropathy) in the feet, meaning minor sores can go unnoticed and turn into major wounds if not checked daily. Essential nursing wisdom!

question: Why is it so important to talk about family planning before discharging a post-abortion care patient?

options.A: Contraceptives cure existing pelvic infections
options.B: Hospital policy mandates permanent sterilization
options.C: It prevents the onset of menopausal symptoms
options.D: Fertility can return very quickly after a termination

explanation: Brilliant! Ovulation can start as early as two weeks after an abortion, so counseling helps prevent unplanned repeat pregnancies.

question: What does 'cohorting' mean in the ward?

options.A: Placing patients with the same infection in the same room
options.B: Training new nursing students in isolation procedures
options.C: Sharing medical equipment between different hospital wards
options.D: Moving a patient to a room with negative air pressure

explanation: When single rooms run out, grouping patients with the exact same infection together is a smart way to manage space and safety.
